AudioBeatGridRequest.description:
Request body for POST /api/analyze/audio.

Only an ``audio_url`` is accepted, on purpose. This service just REMOVED
every caller-supplied filesystem path from its request surface
(``AnalysisRequest.video_path``, ``ReferenceImage.path`` — see the module
docstring), and a new endpoint must not reintroduce the same class of
unconfined read through a different field name. ``s3://`` is refused for the
same reason it is refused elsewhere: the SSRF guard only reasons about
HTTP(S), so a non-HTTP scheme would reach the fetcher un-judged.

The *scheme* check lives here so an obviously-wrong body fails validation
(422) without work. The real judgement — DNS resolution, private/reserved
address ranges, internal-suffix blocklist, and the pin that closes the
rebind window — is ``url_security.validate_public_url``, invoked by
``VideoDownloader.download`` exactly as it is for ``video_url``. It is NOT
called here: it does blocking DNS, and pydantic validation runs on the event
loop.

audio_url.description: HTTP(S) URL of the audio (or video) file to analyse
audio_url.title: Audio Url

meter.description: Beats per bar used for downbeat phase inference (4 = 4/4)
meter.title: Meter

frame_analyses_partial.description: True when ``frame_analyses`` holds only the frames scored before the job stopped — i.e. the job is still running, or reached a terminal state other than 'completed' (failure, cost cap, wall-clock deadline). Use this to tell 'nothing to report' (frame_analyses null/empty, partial False) from 'I was cut off after N frames' (N entries, partial True).

post.description:
Create a new analysis job from a JSON body (video_url).

Local filesystem inputs are not accepted here — ``video_path`` was removed
(arbitrary pod-file read); use this endpoint with ``video_url`` or
``POST /analyze/upload`` for a local file.

The "must carry a source" rule now lives on ``AnalysisRequest`` itself
(``_require_a_source``) rather than in this handler, so no other caller of
the model can build a sourceless request. Consequence: a body with no
``video_url`` is rejected during body validation and returns **422**, the
FastAPI-standard code, where this handler used to hand-roll a 400.

Detect a beat grid (bpm, beats, downbeats, onsets) for a music track.

SYNCHRONOUS — and deliberately unlike every sibling route on this router,
which answers 202 with a ``job_id`` and makes the caller poll. The reason is
the shape of the work, not consistency for its own sake:

* it is seconds, not minutes. A warm process analyses a full track in
  ~0.3s (ffmpeg decode) + ~0.04s (librosa). The 202/poll pattern exists for
  the multi-minute vision+OCR+transcription pipeline; wrapping a sub-second
  computation in a job row, a queue hop, a poll loop and a DB round-trip
  would cost more latency than the analysis itself;
* the caller is a *composer* — the cut-to-beat product needs the grid in
  hand before it can lay out a single edit, so it blocks either way. Making
  it poll only moves the blocking into a loop;
* there is no artifact and nothing to resume. The result is a few hundred
  floats returned in the response body, so no job row, no object-store
  write, and nothing to strand if the pod dies mid-request.

The duration guard is what keeps that choice safe: input longer than
``beat_detector.MAX_DURATION_S`` is refused (413) off the ffprobe header,
before a single sample is decoded, so no request can pin a CPU indefinitely.
Accept a multipart upload + optional JSON config and schedule analysis.

delete.description:
Delete a job, its DB row, and all artifacts (tenant-scoped).

The repo's tenant-scoped ``delete()`` returns False for a wrong-tenant
or missing row, which we map to 404 — same shape as a true miss.

get.description:
Poll the status/progress of an analysis job (tenant-scoped).

Reaps the job first if it has been abandoned. A job whose owning pod died mid-run
keeps its non-terminal status forever (no handler runs), so a poller waits on work
nobody is doing — measured 2026-08-04: 23 such rows, oldest ~11 days. Reaping on the
POLL is what makes it visible to the one caller who is actually asking; a background
sweep would need to read across tenants, which RLS correctly forbids this role.
Stream a single artifact file by logical name (tenant-scoped).
Fetch the full result of a completed (or in-progress) job (tenant-scoped).
Return the verification report for a job that ran with criteria (tenant-scoped).
Return combined DB + API + executor + sweeper + beat-detector health.

Kubernetes readiness probe.

The pipeline runner, the sweeper and the beat detector are deliberately NOT
checked here:

* **A missing PipelineRunner is a build-time fault, so it is shared.** It
  comes from an import that failed against the image — which means it failed
  identically on every replica. Failing readiness would evict the entire
  Deployment at once, taking down status polling, results, verification and
  artifact download for every job already in flight, on top of an executor
  outage. Blindness is bad; deleting the read surface too is worse.
* **The sweeper is a background janitor.** It repairs rows; it serves no
  request. Nothing about a request is wrong when it is dead.
* **The beat detector is one endpoint of several.** Video analysis (pipeline,
  OCR, vision) is unaffected by a failed numba warm-up, and that endpoint
  already answers an honest 503 on its own.

So all three land on ``/health`` — ``unhealthy`` for the executor, ``degraded``
for the other two — loud to an operator and to alerting, inert to the
scheduler. Readiness stays what it can honestly assert: this pod can reach
its database and serve HTTP.
Modern K8s liveness probe path (alias of /health/live).
Modern K8s readiness probe path (alias of /health/ready).
